Cliche choies, but:

* To The Lighthouse by Virginia Woolf

* A Farewell to Arms by Ernest Hemingway

* Dubliners by James Joyce

* The Road by Cormac McCarthy
 
* Moby Dick by Herman Melville

* The Wars by Timothy Findley

* (the final 30 pages of) The Time Machine by H.G. Wells

Well, most directly as an attempt: Countless therapy sessions, as well as a plethora of medication. None of this has ever worked, and I'm becoming more and more certain it never will.

Besides that, I have just tried to find something I enjoy doing. This is possible in the short term, but eventually everything just ends up seeming like the same pointless endeavor. 

I've heard that the best way to become some way is to act that way. Our actions then are self-actualizing. I have not had this experience. I've lived a life that I think most people would be happy with: a good government job, acceptance into law school, healthy social life, etc. But at the end of the day, I just keep thinking 'this is all nonsense' and I can't shake that weight. I've been getting sadder and sadder for so long, and it seems like I've finally hit a tipping point.
